leftEvidence.title: John speaks of beholding the Word’s glory

points.label: Event action and claim
points.left: The Word becomes flesh and dwells among people; the witness says, “We saw his glory,” as of the Father’s only Son.
points.right: After six days Jesus takes three disciples up a high mountain; his face shines, his clothes become white, and Moses and Elijah appear speaking with him.

points.label: Response and consequence
points.left: Grace and truth, Moses, law, and the Son who makes God known are held together.
points.right: Peter proposes three tents; a bright cloud overshadows them, the voice names the beloved Son and commands listening, and the frightened disciples finally see Jesus alone.

payload.posture: John and Matthew both join seen glory with unique Son-language.

rightEvidence.title: Jesus is transfigured before Peter, James, and John

payload.tension: John does not name the mountain, so the relationship remains possible development rather than explicit event memory.
payload.title: Seen glory and narrated mountain glory
